title: spring proxies
goal: 1.5.3 How Spring proxies add runtime behavior

tasks.do: Define what a proxy is and how it relates to the target object.
Contrast JDK dynamic proxies and CGLIB proxies by mechanism, not just name.
State Spring's default selection rule, and Spring Boot's override of it.
Explain which `BeanPostProcessor` substitutes the proxy and at which step.
List three ways to work around self-invocation, with trade-offs.
List every method kind that cannot be advised by a proxy.
Explain why injecting a JDK-proxied bean by concrete class fails.
Explain where field state lives on a CGLIB-proxied bean.
Detect the proxy type at runtime with `AopUtils`.
State how AspectJ weaving avoids these limitations.
Self-invocation runs NO advice — the most-tested consequence.
`final` methods and classes are silently unadvised under CGLIB.
`@Transactional` on a non-public method is ignored by proxy-based AOP.
Spring Boot forces CGLIB; plain Spring prefers JDK proxies when interfaces exist.
The proxy's own fields are uninitialised — state lives on the target.
